messages.author: 71cefeaaa3659875
messages.subject: Re: Error in correctReadDepth predLoess
parts:
Hi Jouni,

Sorry for the delay in responding to your issue.  

Can you check on a few things?
1) Make sure there are no NA's in the tumour or normal wig files after running "wigToRangedData()"; these bins should just be 0.  
2) Do the lines in each wig file "fixedStep chrom=chr1 ..." all use the same naming convention?  It should be handled with the "genomeStyle" argument but just double-check.
3) You can also try to debug the function "correctReadDepth" directly and checking the "tumor_reads" variable prior to running 
tumour_copy <- correctReadcount(tumour_reads, samplesize = samplesize)

Hope this helps,
Gavin

messages.author: 0387a0f27223c740
messages.subject: Re: Error in correctReadDepth predLoess
parts:
Hi Gavin and thank you for your reply!

I have checked the few things you suggested;

1) There are no NA's in the normal or tumor wig files after running "wigToRangedData()". I checked the files visually and by using "grep" command in Linux without any problems. All bins in these files have a value of 0 or larger.
2) All lines in each wig file follow the same naming convention. However, I noticed that in the map wig file the order of lines is different. For example, all other wig files start with line fixedStep chrom=chrM... while map wig starts with line fixedStep chrom=chr1...
3) I tried to debug the function "correctReadDepth" and checked the "tumor_reads" variable prior to running. Please see these files as an attachment In my opinion, the only visible problem in my data is that I have some exons with 0 coverage. Could this be the problem or how does TitanCNA work with these regions?

messages.author: 71cefeaaa3659875
messages.subject: Re: Error in correctReadDepth predLoess
parts:
Hi Jouni,

TITAN will not work on a dataset with such few genes covered.  This is the reason you are seeing the error in the loess correction.

Best,
Gavin
